**Why?**

1. **Where the shadow falls.**  
   A shadow is cast opposite the direction of the light source.  
   If the sun is in the eastern sky (as it is right after sunrise), the sunlight comes from the east, so the shadow falls toward the west.

2. **The “right‑hand side” orientation.**  
   When a person stands facing a pole, the side that is exactly to his right is the direction that is 90° clockwise from the direction he is facing.  
   - If his right side is west, then he must be facing south (because from facing south, your right is west).  
   - If he were facing south, the pole would be in front of him, and the shadow would fall to his right (west).

3. **Putting the two facts together.**  
   The shadow of the pole is exactly to his right → his right side is west.  
   The sun is “after sunrise” → the sun is coming from the east → the shadow points west.  

Therefore, the direction towards which the shadow was pointing at that morning was **west**.
